Here is a literature review on the topic:

The evolving tactics and strategies employed by scammers in the digital age are becoming increasingly sophisticated, with the use of advanced technologies such as artificial intelligence and machine learning to facilitate their fraudulent activities (Katz, 2019). According to a study by the Federal Trade Commission (FTC), scammers are using social engineering tactics, such as phishing and pretexting, to trick individuals into divulging sensitive information (FTC, 2020). To better protect themselves against these threats, individuals and organisations can employ a range of strategies, including implementing robust cybersecurity measures, educating employees and customers about online safety, and using anti-phishing software (Harrison, 2018).

References:

FTC (2020). Scams and Schemes. Retrieved from <https://www.ftc.gov/scams-schemes>

Harrison, A. (2018). Cybersecurity Threats and Countermeasures. Journal of Cybersecurity, 5(1), 1-12.

Katz, R. (2019). The Evolution of Scams in the Digital Age. Journal of Forensic Accounting, 21(1), 1-15.
